title: Soft admission lanes for tiered traffic: per-customer credit aging and elastic spillover
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers across free / paid / enterprise tiers experience hard rejections once their account credit bucket is exhausted. Hard demotions cause poor UX for bursty workloads and create thundering fallbacks to lower-quality model variants or increased latency due to regional failovers. We need a mechanism that: 1) preserves end-user quality for short bursts, 2) enforces long-term quota fairness, and 3) gracefully spills traffic between tiers/regions/model-variants when capacity or credits are constrained.

Proposal: Implement a soft admission layer ("admission shim") in the request router that maintains a per-customer credit ledger with credit-aging and short-duration grace lanes. Key ideas: credit aging will slowly replenish (or age out) reserved credits for customers who have not consumed tokens recently; grace lanes let requests consume a small bounded overage for low-latency short bursts; elastic spillover windows allow tiered traffic to move to a limited set of fallback model variants or adjacent regions when preferred capacity is temporarily insufficient. The admission shim will also emit observability signals and per-request decision metadata for Console tracing and billing reconciliation.

Scope: Implement server-side admission logic and feature flags for gradual rollout. This ticket covers router admission logic, credit ledger APIs, metrics/trace hooks, and initial canary rollout. Follow-up tickets will add UI in Console and billing reconciliation hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Router admits requests within configured grace budgets when a customer is within a short-burst window and emits admission_reason=grace_lane.
2) Customers cannot exceed configured overage caps (tokens-per-minute and tokens-per-24h).
3) Credit aging reduces reserved overage allowance after a configurable inactivity window.
4) When primary capacity unavailable, router prefers: same-region fallback variant -> regional spill -> lower-tier compatible model variant, honoring tier weightings.
5) All admission decisions include metadata (tier, remaining_credits, admission_reason, fallback_used) and are persisted to trace logs and metrics.
6) No client-visible 500s introduced during canary.
7) End-to-end load test shows <10% increase in p95 latency for grace-admitted requests and no SLO regressions for enterprise customers.
implementation_notes:
- Add lightweight in-memory credit ledger sharded by customer_id with persistent checkpointing to Dynamo-like store every 30s.
- Credit aging policy: exponential decay with configurable half-life (default 6h) for overage allowance.
- Grace lane policy: token-based micro-credits (default 500 tokens/min burst, 10k tokens/day cap for overage) per account; configurable per-plan override.
- Admission decision flow: check quota -> if exhausted, check grace lane budget -> if not available, evaluate fallback chain (local-region compatible model variants with quality rank) -> record decision and route.
- Expose flags: enable_grace_lane, grace_budget_multiplier, aging_half_life, fallback_window_ms.
- Add unit tests for ledger mutation, race conditions, and durability semantics.
- Add circuit-breaker guard to disable grace lanes automatically when cluster-level overload > 85%.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: ledger add/spend/age/resume semantics, concurrency tests (1000 concurrent claims).
- Integration tests: simulate tiered traffic patterns (free burst, paid sustained, enterprise large) and assert admission decisions and metric emissions.
- Load test: k6 scenario reproducing production-like mix to verify p50/p95/p99 impact; run against canary cluster.
- Chaos test: simulate persistence store lag and verify router falls back to conservative mode (no grace lanes).
- QA checklist: verify trace fields in Console, ensure billing event emitted for overage consumption.
- Test owners: Jin Park (unit/integration), Priya Sharma (load/chaos).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag rollout to internal staging. 2) Canary 1% traffic for non-enterprise customers for 48h. Monitor error rates, latency, and grace_admit ratio. 3) Increase to 10% after safety window and manual review of metrics. 4) Regional canary: enable in us-west-2 only for additional 48h. 5) Full rollout for free/paid once stable; enterprise remains opt-in until customer SLAs validated.
- Automated rollback: toggle enable_grace_lane=false and revert checkpointing writes; automation runbook in /runbooks/grace-lane-rollback.md.
rollbacks:
- Immediate flag flip to disable grace lanes.
- Rehydrate ledger from last persisted snapshot for reconciliation.
- Revert routing PR if unexpected regressions in enterprise SLOs.
- Postmortem and customer outreach template prepared in Confluence if high-impact discovered.
